intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A top eco-adventure that puts you eye-level with toucans, howler monkeys, and rare orchids.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through jungle canals in a small boat guided by a certified naturalist, spotting caimans, river turtles, poison dart frogs, manatees, and over 300 bird species. If visiting July–October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hike and Hot Springs Soak
experiences.description: Trek lava fields and rainforest trails around the iconic Arenal Volcano with a naturalist guide, then unwind in natural geothermal hot springs fed by the volcano's heat. Spot howler monkeys, coatis, and exotic birds along the trail before relaxing under jungle canopy at dusk.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning for hiking, Evening for hot springs

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Walk
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse parks with a professional guide and high-powered spotting scope. Encounter three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and iguanas, then cool off on the park's stunning white-sand beaches framed by lush rainforest.

experiences.name: Corcovado Rainforest Kayaking and Mangrove Exploration
experiences.description: Paddle through pristine mangrove estuaries and coastal waterways bordering Corcovado National Park — dubbed the most biologically intense place on Earth by National Geographic. Spot tapirs, scarlet macaws, bull sharks, and nesting crocodiles while your guide shares deep knowledge of this irreplaceable ecosystem.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange currency at the airport (look for Banco Nacional for better rates). Take a shared shuttle or public bus to Aegean Bliss Resort to save on transport costs. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed walk along the beachfront to get oriented with the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest local town on foot. Visit a nearby 'soda' (traditional Costa Rican small restaurant) for your first authentic meal. Grab a cold Imperial or Pilsen beer and enjoy the sunset from the beach near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick 'casado' (rice, beans, meat, salad) at a local soda near the airport for around $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local beachside soda — try Gallo Pinto with chicken and fresh juice for under $8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and settling in. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport (Kolbi or Claro) for around $10-15 USD with data. Confirm shuttle bookings for upcoming days at the resort's front desk.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a free sunrise beach walk along the resort's beachfront. Look for coastal wildlife including pelicans, herons, and hermit crabs. Enjoy the peaceful morning atmosphere before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife reserve accessible from the resort area. Explore marked trails on foot to spot monkeys, sloths, toucans, and iguanas. Bring water and sunscreen. Many parks charge $18 USD entry — budget accordingly.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Cook or assemble a simple meal from a local 'pulpería' (corner store) to save money, or dine at a budget soda. Sit on the beach and stargaze — Costa Rica's skies away from the city are spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Gallo Pinto with eggs and fresh fruit at the resort or a nearby soda — $4-6 USD
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local pulpería — bread, cheese, fruit, and water for under $5 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda dinner — try Olla de Carne (beef and vegetable soup) with rice for $6-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wear insect repellent and closed-toe shoes for trail walks. Bring a reusable water bottle to refill and reduce plastic waste. February is dry season in most of Costa Rica — expect warm, sunny weather.

day_by_day.morning: Book an early morning guided wildlife tour in the local area. Look for budget group tours offered at the resort or nearby tour operators — group rates can be as low as $25-35 USD per person. Focus on birdwatching and spotting howler monkeys and sloths in the tree canopy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby mangrove estuary or river for a self-guided kayak or canoe experience. Many areas offer affordable rentals ($10-15 USD/hour). Paddle through the mangroves and look for crocodiles, birds, and tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event in the nearest town — check local bulletin boards. Alternatively, enjoy a beachfire gathering if permitted, or join other budget travelers at a hostel's social area for tips and company.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit plate and coffee from a street vendor — $3-4 USD
meals.lunch: Casado plate at a local restaurant — $6-8 USD
meals.dinner: Try a local 'marisquería' (seafood restaurant) for fresh catch of the day with rice and beans — $10-12 USD (a slight splurge worth it for freshness)

day_by_day.notes: Book kayak rentals in advance during peak season (February). Bring dry bags or waterproof pouches for your phone and valuables during water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Zip-lining day! Book a budget zip-line tour with a local operator — prices range from $35-60 USD depending on the number of platforms and location. Look for combo deals that include canopy tours and hanging bridges. Depart early to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, visit a nearby hanging bridges trail or suspension bridge walkway through the forest canopy. These offer incredible wildlife viewing opportunities from above — look for toucans, monkeys, and colorful frogs. Entry is typically $15-25 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover at the resort. Treat sore muscles with a swim in the ocean or resort pool. Head to a casual beachside bar for a happy hour drink (Imperial beer ~$2-3 USD) and watch the sunset.

meals.breakfast: Pinto breakfast at the resort or nearby café — $4-5 USD. Eat well before the physical activity.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the zip-line tour. Many operators include a light snack — confirm when booking.
meals.dinner: Budget pizza or pasta at a tourist-area restaurant for $8-10 USD, or cook simple pasta from pulpería groceries

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing for zip-lining. Secure loose items — GoPro mounts are usually available to rent. Avoid booking the cheapest operators with no safety reviews; read TripAdvisor reviews first.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided nature walk along the beach at low tide. Explore tide pools for sea stars, crabs, and small fish. Collect shells and observe shorebirds. This is one of the best free eco-adventures available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local butterfly garden or reptile sanctuary — many charge $10-15 USD entry. These are excellent for up-close wildlife encounters including poison dart frogs, snakes, turtles, and hundreds of butterfly species.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local night market or artisan fair if available. Purchase handmade souvenirs directly from artisans for better prices. Try local street food snacks like 'churros' or 'empanadas' for $1-2 USD each.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh juice with toast from a beach café — $4-6 USD
meals.lunch: Roadside 'chifrijo' (rice, beans, pork, pico de gallo) at a local bar — $5-6 USD
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal from the local market — buy fresh vegetables, rice, and beans for a simple stir-fry for under $5 USD total

day_by_day.notes: Tide pool exploration is best 1-2 hours before and after low tide — check a tide chart online or ask locals. Be careful not to step on or remove any marine life.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby national park or protected wildlife area (plan for a full morning). Hire a local guide for $20-30 USD — their expertise dramatically increases wildlife sightings. Look for scarlet macaws, toucans, coatis, and potentially a jaguar track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming and snorkeling at a nearby beach. Rent snorkel gear for $5-10 USD and explore the underwater world — colorful reef fish, sea turtles, and rays are commonly spotted in February.
day_by_day.evening: Join a budget group tour for a night wildlife walk ($20-30 USD). Costa Rica's nocturnal wildlife is extraordinary — red-eyed tree frogs, kinkajous, armadillos, and sleeping birds are commonly spotted.

meals.breakfast: Gallo Pinto with natilla (sour cream) and fresh orange juice — $4-5 USD
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from the pulpería — sandwiches, fruit, and water for $4-5 USD to eat at the park
meals.dinner: Post-night-walk meal at a local soda — try Sopa Negra (black bean soup) with egg for $5-7 USD

day_by_day.notes: For the night walk, wear long pants and closed shoes to protect against insects. Bring a red-light headlamp as white light disturbs wildlife. Book in advance as group spots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and relaxation morning at the resort beach. Practice yoga on the beach (many resorts offer free or low-cost sessions), swim, read, and recharge midway through the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or permaculture project for a guided tour ($10-20 USD). Learn about sustainable agriculture in Costa Rica, taste tropical fruits like rambutan, starfruit, and cacao straight from the source.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate the halfway point of your trip. Find a restaurant with fresh ceviche and local fish — budget $15-18 USD for a sit-down meal with a drink.

meals.breakfast: Full resort or café breakfast — treat yourself to a big meal since it's a rest day — $6-8 USD
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut water ($2 USD) and tropical fruit from a beach vendor — light and refreshing
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant — fresh ceviche starter and grilled fish main with plantains — $15-18 USD

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally lighter to prevent burnout on a 13-day trip. Use this time to do laundry (many laundromats charge $5-8 USD per load), restock supplies, and plan the second week's logistics.

day_by_day.morning: Book an early morning boat tour of a nearby river, estuary, or coastal waterway ($25-40 USD). These tours are exceptional for wildlife — crocodiles, caimans, river otters, kingfishers, and herons are commonly seen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local waterfall accessible by a short hike. Many waterfalls in Costa Rica are free or charge a small entry fee ($5-10 USD). Swim in the natural pool at the base — one of the most refreshing experiences in the country.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free community event, local football match, or simply walk through the town plaza. Grab a 'raspado' (shaved ice with tropical syrup) for $1-2 USD and people-watch.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the boat tour — rice and eggs at a soda — $4-5 USD
meals.lunch: Picnic at the waterfall — buy food from the local market beforehand — $4-5 USD
meals.dinner: Try 'arroz con pollo' (rice with chicken) at a family-run soda — $6-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Confirm waterfall trail conditions and accessibility before going — some require a 4WD vehicle or guided access. Bring a change of clothes and a towel for swimming. Waterfalls can be slippery — wear water shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Second zip-lining or canopy adventure, this time at a different location or a more advanced course if available. Some areas offer canyoning or rappelling down waterfalls as add-ons ($15-25 USD extra) — highly recommended for thrill-seekers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local wildlife rescue and rehabilitation center ($15-20 USD entry). These centers house injured or orphaned animals including sloths, monkeys, toucans, and big cats. Your entry fee directly supports animal welfare.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a group meal if staying with other travelers — buy fresh ingredients from the local market and prepare a simple Costa Rican-inspired meal. Share stories and tips with fellow budget travelers.

meals.breakfast: Energy-rich breakfast before zip-lining — banana pancakes at a café — $5-6 USD
meals.lunch: Many wildlife centers have a small café — budget $6-8 USD for a simple lunch there
meals.dinner: Group self-catered dinner from local market ingredients — $4-6 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: At wildlife rescue centers, follow all rules — do not touch animals unless specifically guided to. Photography rules vary — always ask first. These centers often need volunteers; ask about short-term volunteer opportunities if interested.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk — Costa Rica has over 900 bird species. Hire a local birding guide ($20-30 USD) or join a group tour. February is excellent for spotting migratory birds alongside resident species. Bring binoculars if you have them.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach that's less touristy and more secluded — ask locals or the resort staff for recommendations. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and exploring the coastline on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset kayaking or stand-up paddleboard session ($10-15 USD rental) along the coastline. The golden hour light on the water is spectacular and wildlife activity increases at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Pre-birdwatching light breakfast — coffee and 'pan dulce' (sweet bread) from a bakery — $2-3 USD
meals.lunch: Beach picnic — fresh bread, local cheese, fruit, and juice from a pulpería — $5-6 USD
meals.dinner: Beachside BBQ if available, or a local seafood soda — grilled shrimp with rice — $9-11 USD

day_by_day.notes: The best birdwatching is in the first 2 hours after sunrise. Wear neutral-colored clothing to avoid startling birds. Free birding apps like Merlin Bird ID (Cornell Lab) are excellent companions for self-guided birdwatching.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day eco-adventure hike in a nearby protected area or national park. Choose a trail rated moderate to challenging for the best wildlife and scenery. Look for white-faced capuchins, howler monkeys, and coatis along the trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hike or find a scenic viewpoint for lunch with panoramic views. Many trails lead to lookout points over the coastline or rainforest canopy — take your time and enjoy the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area tired but fulfilled. Treat yourself to a local massage ($20-30 USD for 60 minutes at a budget spa) to recover from the day's hike.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before the long hike — full casado breakfast with eggs, beans, rice, and fruit — $5-7 USD
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — energy bars, fruit, nuts, and sandwiches prepared the night before — $4-5 USD
meals.dinner: Post-hike reward meal — try a local 'fritanga' (fried food platter) with yuca, plantains, and chicken — $8-10 USD

day_by_day.notes: For long hikes, bring at least 2 liters of water, sunscreen, insect repellent, a basic first aid kit, and a fully charged phone with offline maps downloaded. Tell the resort or a friend your planned trail and expected return time.

day_by_day.morning: Final wildlife experience — book a morning turtle or marine wildlife tour if available in the area ($25-40 USD). February may offer opportunities to see nesting or hatching sea turtles depending on the location. Alternatively, take a final snorkeling trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping at local artisan markets — buy directly from makers for authentic, fairly priced crafts. Look for handmade jewelry, carved wood items, and locally produced coffee ($5-10 USD per bag of premium Costa Rican coffee makes an excellent gift).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the nicest restaurant you've visited during the trip — a final splurge to celebrate an incredible 13 days. Enjoy a full Costa Rican meal with fresh seafood, tropical sides, and a local dessert like 'tres leches' cake.

meals.breakfast: Final big breakfast — smoothie, eggs, Gallo Pinto, and fresh tropical fruit plate — $6-8 USD
meals.lunch: Light lunch while shopping — street tacos or empanadas from a market stall — $3-5 USD
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — budget $18-25 USD for a memorable final meal with fresh fish, plantains, and local dessert

day_by_day.notes: When buying coffee, look for '100% Costa Rican' labels and single-origin bags. Avoid airport souvenir shops — prices are 2-3x higher than local markets. Pack souvenirs carefully to protect fragile items during the flight home.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — take photos, reflect on the journey, and say goodbye to the ocean. Enjoy a slow, peaceful breakfast. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and ensure all belongings are packed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either head directly to the airport via shared shuttle (book in advance — $15-25 USD shared vs $60-80 USD private taxi) or squeeze in one final activity near the airport area such as visiting a local coffee shop or browsing a market.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of eco-adventures, wildlife encounters, and zip-lining through the rainforest canopy. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final Costa Rican breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — savor the Gallo Pinto one last time — $4-6 USD
meals.lunch: Light airport meal or snacks purchased beforehand from a local market — $5-8 USD
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Keep $29 USD cash available if the airport exit tax is not included in your ticket (most modern tickets include it, but verify). Take one last look at the mountains and coastline — Costa Rica has a way of calling travelers back. ¡Pura Vida!

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A top eco-adventure that puts you eye-level with toucans, howler monkeys, and rare orchids.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Walk
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse parks with a professional guide and high-powered spotting scope. Encounter three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and iguanas, then cool off on the park's stunning white-sand beaches framed by lush rainforest.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and meet private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the scenic drive (approx. 3–4 hours depending on resort location). Stop at a roadside fruit stand to sample fresh tropical fruits like maracuyá and cas.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront. Take a leisurely stroll along the beach at sunset to decompress from travel. Explore the resort grounds and get oriented with amenities.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport — Musmanni Bakery in the airport terminal offers affordable sandwiches and pastries
meals.lunch: Light snack at airport or roadside stop during transfer
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant — try the Casado (traditional Costa Rican plate with rice, beans, plantains, and fresh fish) — budget approx. $18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings with the resort concierge upon check-in. Exchange currency or withdraw colones from the airport ATM before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided sunrise beach walk along the resort's coastline. Watch for shore birds, hermit crabs, and possibly nesting sea turtles depending on the season. Enjoy a hearty breakfast at the resort before the day begins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a local guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboard tour in the calm coastal waters near the resort. Paddle through mangrove estuaries and look for herons, kingfishers, and crocodiles from a safe distance. Tour typically lasts 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort pool as the sun sets. Head into the nearest town for a casual dinner at a local soda (family-run Costa Rican restaurant) to experience authentic local cuisine at an affordable price.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast buffet at the resort — fresh tropical fruit, gallo pinto, eggs, and local coffee ($10–15)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack bar near the kayak launch point — fresh coconut water and empanadas
meals.dinner: Local soda in town — Gallo pinto, fried plantains, chicken or fish, and a Pilsen beer — approx. $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the kayaking/SUP tour through the resort concierge the night before. Apply reef-safe sunscreen and bring a dry bag for electronics. Mangrove tours are best done in the morning but afternoon slots are also available.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife spotting walk along the nearby nature trail or beach forest edge. Look for howler monkeys, scarlet macaws, and iguanas that are most active at dawn. Bring binoculars if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local wildlife rescue center or nature reserve. Many centers in Costa Rica allow visitors to observe rehabilitated sloths, toucans, and coatis up close. This is an ethical and educational wildlife experience that supports conservation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a swim and sunset cocktail on the beach. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort's casual beachside grill.

meals.breakfast: Café style breakfast at a local bakery near the resort — fresh pan dulce, coffee, and fresh juice ($6–10)
meals.lunch: At the wildlife rescue center's café or a nearby rancho-style restaurant — casado or fresh ceviche ($10–14)
meals.dinner: Resort beachside grill — grilled mahi-mahi with coconut rice and a tropical salad ($20–28)

day_by_day.notes: Check the wildlife rescue center's opening hours in advance and confirm they accept walk-ins or require reservations. Wear neutral-colored clothing and closed-toe shoes for nature walks. Avoid feeding any wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion begins — depart early for Manuel Antonio National Park (travel time varies by resort location, typically 30–90 minutes). Arrive at park opening (7:00 AM) for the best wildlife sightings before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Walk — Explore one of the world's most biodiverse parks with a professional guide and high-powered spotting scopes. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and hundreds of bird species. After the guided walk, relax on Playa Manuel Antonio — one of Costa Rica's most beautiful beaches inside the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and head out for dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the nearest town, celebrating a fantastic day of wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — grab gallo pinto and eggs to go if needed
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch inside the park or at the park entrance area — bring your own or purchase from vendors outside the gate ($8–12)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in town — try a seafood platter or traditional arroz con pollo ($15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park limits daily visitors — book your park entry tickets online in advance at sinac.go.cr. The guided wildlife walk is one of your pre-booked experiences. Bring plenty of water, insect repellent, and a rain jacket. The park closes on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at the resort. Enjoy the beachfront, swim in the ocean, or take a yoga class if offered by the resort. This is a recovery day after the active park excursion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon snorkeling tour along the nearby coral reef or rocky coastline. Explore colorful fish, sea urchins, and possibly spotted eagle rays. Many resorts offer snorkeling gear rental and guided tours.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran cruise along the coastline — a classic Costa Rica experience with music, drinks, and stunning Pacific views. Look for dolphins and flying fish alongside the boat.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — smoothie bowl, fresh fruit, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch at the resort — fish tacos, fresh ceviche, and a cold Imperial beer ($14–18)
meals.dinner: Light dinner included or available on the catamaran cruise, or dine at a beachfront restaurant post-cruise — grilled shrimp skewers and plantain chips ($18–24)

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset catamaran cruise through the resort concierge — popular tours fill up quickly, especially on Fridays. Bring a light jacket for the evening sea breeze. The snorkeling tour is best done in the afternoon when waters tend to be calmer.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — depart resort after breakfast and head toward Monteverde Cloud Forest region (approx. 4–5 hour drive or shorter by 4x4 on unpaved mountain roads). The journey itself is an adventure through coffee plantations and misty mountain terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Monteverde / Santa Elena area. Check in to a mid-range cloud forest lodge or eco-hotel. Take a short walk through the town of Santa Elena to get oriented, visit local artisan shops, and pick up any supplies needed.
day_by_day.evening: Join a guided night walk in the Monteverde area to spot nocturnal wildlife — glass frogs, tarantulas, red-eyed tree frogs, kinkajous, and owls. Night walks are one of the most unique wildlife experiences in Costa Rica.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before checkout
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside restaurant or soda during the mountain drive — typical Costa Rican lunch plate ($8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Santa Elena town center — try Morpho's Restaurant or a similar local favorite known for hearty vegetarian and meat dishes ($14–20)

day_by_day.notes: The road to Monteverde can be rough — confirm whether a 4x4 vehicle is needed for your route. Alternatively, a shared shuttle service (approx. $30–45 per person) is available from major hubs. Book your Monteverde accommodation in advance as it fills quickly on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. The tour typically includes 10–15 cables, Tarzan swings, and hanging bridges with breathtaking views above the treetops. Operators like Original Canopy Tour or Selvatura Park offer world-class experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the zip-line adrenaline rush, visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a self-guided or guided walk through the primary forest. Look for resplendent quetzals (February is peak quetzal season!), bellbirds, and emerald toucanets.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the lodge and reflect on the day's adventures. Visit a local café in Santa Elena for coffee tasting — Monteverde is renowned for its high-altitude shade-grown coffee.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before the zip-line tour — eggs, gallo pinto, and strong Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Post-zip-line lunch at a café near the reserve entrance — sandwiches, soup, and fresh juice ($10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sabor Tico in Santa Elena or similar local restaurant — casado with grilled chicken or fish ($12–18)

day_by_day.notes: The zip-line tour is one of your pre-booked experiences. Wear closed-toe shoes, long pants recommended, and leave jewelry at the lodge. February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal in Monteverde — ask your guide specifically about quetzal sightings. Bring a light rain jacket as the cloud forest is frequently misty.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided birdwatching tour in the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve. February is excellent for birding with over 400 species recorded in the area. A specialist guide will help you spot rare species like the three-wattled bellbird and golden-browed chlorophonia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and/or the Reptile House — excellent complementary wildlife experiences that are educational and photogenic. The butterfly garden houses dozens of tropical species including the brilliant Blue Morpho.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Costa Rican cooking class in Santa Elena — learn to make gallo pinto, ceviche, and tres leches cake with local ingredients. A fun and culturally immersive evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the birdwatching tour — fruit, granola, and coffee at the lodge
meals.lunch: Lunch at the butterfly garden café or nearby soda — typical casado or sandwich ($9–13)
meals.dinner: Dishes prepared during the cooking class or a follow-up dinner at a local restaurant — budget $15–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the birdwatching guide in advance through your lodge — early morning (6:00–9:00 AM) is the prime window for bird activity. The cooking class should be reserved ahead of time; check with the Santa Elena visitor center for available classes. Bring a telephoto lens or use binoculars for birdwatching.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Curi-Cancha Wildlife Refuge — a quieter, less-visited alternative to the main Monteverde Reserve that offers excellent wildlife viewing with fewer crowds. Walk the trails and look for coatis, agoutis, and dozens of bird species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day — depart Monteverde and head toward the Arenal Volcano region (approx. 3–4 hours via the lake ferry shortcut across Lago Arenal — a scenic and highly recommended route). Arrive in La Fortuna area by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in natural hot springs near Arenal Volcano — choose from mid-range options like Baldi Hot Springs or Tabacon (book in advance). The volcanic-heated thermal pools are the perfect way to relax after days of adventure.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before checkout
meals.lunch: Lunch in Tilarán or at a lakeside restaurant during the Lago Arenal ferry crossing — fresh tilapia or chicken soup ($10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner in La Fortuna town — Don Rufino Restaurant or a similar mid-range option offering local cuisine ($16–24)

day_by_day.notes: The Lago Arenal lake ferry (Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer) is a popular and scenic shortcut between Monteverde and Arenal — book through your lodge or a local operator ($25–35 per person). Confirm hot springs reservations in advance. Book new accommodation in La Fortuna for the next two nights.

day_by_day.morning: Guided hike in Arenal Volcano National Park — walk through old lava fields and primary rainforest with views of the iconic conical volcano. A knowledgeable guide will explain the 1968 eruption history and point out wildlife along the trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: White-water rafting on the Balsa or Sarapiquí River — a thrilling eco-adventure suitable for most fitness levels. Class II–III rapids offer excitement without being extreme, and the river corridor is rich in wildlife including kingfishers and river otters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna for a relaxed evening. Browse the town's artisan market and enjoy a casual dinner at a local soda or mid-range restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at La Fortuna lodge — fresh fruit, eggs, and gallo pinto
meals.lunch: Lunch included with the rafting tour (most operators provide a riverside meal) or grab a bite in town ($10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a La Fortuna soda or mid-range restaurant — try the chifrijo (rice, beans, pork, and pico de gallo) or fresh palm heart salad ($12–18)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Arenal hike and rafting tour through your La Fortuna accommodation or a local tour operator. Wear sturdy hiking boots for the lava field trail. For rafting, wear quick-dry clothing and secure footwear — waterproof bags are provided by the operator. Both activities can often be combined as a full-day package.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the La Fortuna Waterfall — a stunning 70-meter cascade accessible via a 500-step descent through lush rainforest. Swim in the natural pool at the base (one of the most refreshing experiences in Costa Rica). Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided wildlife safari float on the Peñas Blancas River — a peaceful flat-water river tour by inflatable raft where guides use spotting scopes to find sloths, caimans, basilisk lizards, and a wide variety of tropical birds in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Travel back toward the Pacific coast or central region depending on the resort's location. If returning to Aegean Bliss Resort area, begin the journey (approx. 3–5 hours). Alternatively, spend one final night in La Fortuna.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the waterfall hike — pack energy snacks like granola bars and bananas
meals.lunch: Lunch at the waterfall's on-site restaurant or a nearby soda in La Fortuna ($10–15)
meals.dinner: If traveling, stop at a roadside restaurant en route — or dinner in La Fortuna at Lava Lounge Bar & Grill (mid-range, great burgers and local dishes, $14–20)

day_by_day.notes: The La Fortuna Waterfall charges a small entrance fee (~$18). The descent is steep — take your time and wear non-slip shoes. The wildlife safari float is a gentle activity suitable for all ages and is highly recommended for wildlife photography. Book both activities the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront area (if not already there). Spend the morning enjoying the beach — swimming, sunbathing, and taking in the Pacific views. This is a well-deserved rest morning after an action-packed week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day horseback riding tour through coastal trails and farmland near the resort. Horseback riding is a classic Costa Rican activity that offers a unique perspective of the landscape and is available at most beach destinations.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner at a top-rated local restaurant near the resort — splurge slightly for a memorable last full evening. Enjoy fresh seafood, a bottle of local wine, and toast to an incredible Costa Rica adventure.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed breakfast at a café near the resort or on-site — acai bowl, fresh juice, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Beach club or resort lunch — ceviche, fish tacos, and a cold beer ($14–18)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a mid-to-upper-range beachfront restaurant — whole grilled snapper, lobster, or mixed seafood platter with tropical sides ($25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the horseback riding tour through the resort concierge. Wear long pants and closed-toe shoes for riding. For the farewell dinner, make a reservation earlier in the day as beachfront restaurants fill up quickly on Friday evenings. This is a great evening for reflection and journaling about your trip highlights.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — a peaceful and memorable way to say goodbye to Costa Rica. Take photos, collect a small shell as a memento, and soak in the last moments of the Pacific coast. Enjoy a final Costa Rican breakfast with fresh tropical fruit and a perfect cup of café chorreado (traditional drip coffee).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depart for Juan Santamaría International Airport (allow ample travel time depending on resort location — at least 3–5 hours before flight). Stop at a souvenir shop or artisan market en route to pick up coffee, chocolate, or handcrafted gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure. Arrive at the airport with time to spare. Enjoy a final Imperial beer or cup of Costa Rican coffee at the airport lounge before boarding. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — gallo pinto, fresh fruit, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee (the best in the world!)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a restaurant near the airport — sandwiches, empanadas, or a casado ($10–15)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm flight details and check-in online the night before. Allow extra time for airport security and immigration — San José airport can be busy on weekends. Declare any food items (coffee, chocolate) at customs if returning to countries with strict agricultural rules. Keep a small amount of colones for any last-minute airport purchases. Pura Vida — until next time, Costa Rica!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A top eco-adventure that puts you eye-level with toucans, howler monkeys, and rare orchids.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through jungle canals in a small boat guided by a certified naturalist, spotting caimans, river turtles, poison dart frogs, manatees, and over 300 bird species. If visiting July–October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hike and Hot Springs Soak
experiences.description: Trek lava fields and rainforest trails around the iconic Arenal Volcano with a naturalist guide, then unwind in natural geothermal hot springs fed by the volcano's heat. Spot howler monkeys, coatis, and exotic birds along the trail before relaxing under jungle canopy at dusk.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning for hiking, Evening for hot springs

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Walk
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse parks with a professional guide and high-powered spotting scope. Encounter three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and iguanas, then cool off on the park's stunning white-sand beaches framed by lush rainforest.

experiences.name: Corcovado Rainforest Kayaking and Mangrove Exploration
experiences.description: Paddle through pristine mangrove estuaries and coastal waterways bordering Corcovado National Park — dubbed the most biologically intense place on Earth by National Geographic. Spot tapirs, scarlet macaws, bull sharks, and nesting crocodiles while your guide shares deep knowledge of this irreplaceable ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer via luxury SUV to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome cocktail and resort orientation. Settle into your beachfront suite, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to decompress after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's ocean-facing bar, followed by a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's signature beachfront restaurant. Take the evening slowly to acclimate to Costa Rica's time zone and tropical atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light snack or airport lounge meal prior to departure / en route
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort Signature Beachfront Restaurant — fresh ceviche, grilled pargo (red snapper), and tropical fruit dessert paired with a local Guaro Sour cocktail

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through the resort's concierge. Request early check-in if possible. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with the concierge upon arrival. February is dry season — expect warm, sunny weather ideal for outdoor activities.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort, then embark on a Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Walk. A certified naturalist guide will lead you through one of the world's most biodiverse parks with high-powered spotting scopes, searching for white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, scarlet macaws, and poison dart frogs amid lush primary rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Manuel Antonio's pristine beaches within the park boundaries — Playa Biesanz or Playa Manuel Antonio offer crystal-clear waters for a private swim. Return to the resort for a luxurious afternoon at the infinity pool or indulge in a 90-minute couples' massage at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on your private balcony watching the Pacific sunset, followed by dinner at a premium local restaurant in nearby Quepos — La Cantina or Kapi Kapi Restaurant, known for their fusion Costa Rican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — tropical fruits, gallo pinto, eggs benedict, freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the resort chef, enjoyed within Manuel Antonio National Park
meals.dinner: Kapi Kapi Restaurant, Quepos — tasting menu featuring local lobster, plantain-crusted sea bass, and artisanal desserts; wine pairing recommended

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park limits daily visitor numbers — ensure entry tickets are pre-booked through the resort concierge. Wear light breathable clothing, apply reef-safe sunscreen, and bring insect repellent. The park opens at 7:00 AM; an early start maximizes wildlife sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga session on the beach led by the resort's wellness instructor, followed by a gourmet breakfast. Then depart by private charter flight (approximately 45 minutes) or luxury ground transfer toward the Tortuguero region, beginning the journey north along Costa Rica's Caribbean coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tortuguero and board a private luxury canal boat for the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari. Glide silently through jungle waterways with a certified naturalist guide, spotting river caimans, river otters, Jesus Christ lizards, green sea turtles, and an extraordinary array of tropical birds including toucans and herons.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a premium eco-lodge within or near Tortuguero (pre-arranged by concierge — Tortuga Lodge & Gardens recommended for its luxury amenities). Enjoy a candlelit dinner on the lodge's riverside terrace with views over the canals.

meals.breakfast: Resort gourmet breakfast — avocado toast, smoked salmon, fresh tropical juices
meals.lunch: Lunch aboard or at the Tortuga Lodge restaurant — Caribbean rice and beans, fresh fish, plantains
meals.dinner: Tortuga Lodge riverside dinner — Caribbean-style whole snapper, coconut curry shrimp, rum-infused pineapple dessert

day_by_day.notes: This is an overnight excursion away from the main resort — coordinate with the resort concierge to secure your suite for return. Tortuguero is only accessible by boat or small plane; a private charter is the most comfortable option. Pack a small overnight bag with essentials. Mosquito repellent is essential in Tortuguero.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn optional guided walk along Tortuguero beach (February is not primary nesting season, but green sea turtles may still be present). Alternatively, enjoy an early morning bird-watching walk through the lodge's private nature trails with a resident naturalist — over 300 bird species inhabit the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Second guided canal safari focusing on the park's deeper waterways and lagoons, exploring areas not reached the previous day. Return to the lodge for a leisurely lunch, then private transfer back to the airstrip for charter flight back toward the Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, unwind with a refreshing swim in the infinity pool. Enjoy a quiet in-room dining experience on your private terrace — fresh seafood platter and chilled white wine as the sun sets over the Pacific.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at Tortuga Lodge before morning excursion
meals.lunch: Tortuga Lodge farewell lunch — traditional Costa Rican casado with fresh local fish
meals.dinner: In-room private dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated seafood platter, tropical salad, chocolate lava cake, and a bottle of premium Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return charter flight timing with the concierge the evening before. Allow buffer time for water taxi connections in Tortuguero. This two-day Tortuguero excursion is one of the most immersive wildlife experiences in Central America — photography enthusiasts should bring a telephoto lens.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery morning at the resort. Indulge in a late gourmet breakfast followed by a 90-minute deep tissue or hot stone massage at the resort spa. Lounge by the beachfront infinity pool with a good book and tropical cocktails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling or stand-up paddleboard session arranged through the resort's water sports concierge along the protected reef near the resort. A certified marine guide accompanies you to point out tropical fish, sea stars, and coral formations.
day_by_day.evening: Premium sunset catamaran cruise along the Pacific coastline — champagne, artisanal canapés, and spectacular views of the coastline at golden hour. Return to the resort for a fine dining dinner at the resort restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort brunch — eggs any style, smoked meats, pastries, fresh fruit platters, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — ceviche tostadas, grilled corn, fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort fine dining restaurant — seven-course tasting menu featuring Costa Rican ingredients: hearts of palm salad, sea bass tiradito, filet mignon with chimichurri, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day strategically placed mid-trip to recharge before the more adventurous second half. The sunset catamaran should be booked through the resort concierge at least 24 hours in advance. February's dry season offers near-perfect conditions for water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private luxury 4x4 transfer toward the Osa Peninsula and Corcovado region (approximately 2.5–3 hours from the resort). Enjoy a packed gourmet breakfast en route. Upon arrival, board a private kayak with expert guides for the Corcovado Rainforest Kayaking and Mangrove Exploration — paddle through pristine mangrove estuaries teeming with wildlife including scarlet macaws, crocodiles, and howler monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided hike into the buffer zone of Corcovado National Park — one of the most biodiverse places on Earth. With a certified naturalist, search for tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, giant anteaters, and multiple monkey species. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch in a jungle clearing.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a premium eco-lodge near Puerto Jiménez (Lapa Rios Lodge — an iconic luxury eco-resort perched above the rainforest canopy — is highly recommended). Enjoy cocktails on the open-air terrace overlooking the Golfo Dulce at sunset, followed by a farm-to-table dinner.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast box from the resort — croissants, fruit, yogurt, thermos coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet jungle picnic prepared by the lodge — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, tropical fruits, sparkling water
meals.dinner: Lapa Rios Lodge restaurant — organic farm-to-table menu featuring locally sourced ingredients: hearts of palm soup, grilled Osa chicken, cacao-based dessert with locally grown chocolate

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado is one of the most remote and pristine national parks in the Americas — permits must be arranged well in advance through the concierge. Wear sturdy hiking shoes and long lightweight pants. This is another overnight excursion; coordinate with Aegean Bliss Resort to hold your suite.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn bird-watching walk at Lapa Rios Lodge's private reserve with a resident naturalist — the lodge sits within a 1,000-acre private rainforest reserve and is home to over 350 bird species. Scarlet macaws, toucans, and motmots are commonly spotted at sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return journey toward Aegean Bliss Resort via private luxury transfer, stopping at a premium artisan market in Dominical or Uvita for locally made souvenirs, handcrafted jewelry, and organic cacao products. Optional whale-watching boat tour from Uvita (humpback whales are sometimes present February–March in the Marino Ballena National Park area).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a welcome-back cocktail and a relaxed dinner at the resort's beachside grill, savoring fresh catch of the day under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Lapa Rios Lodge breakfast — tropical buffet with local fruits, eggs, gallo pinto, fresh juice
meals.lunch: Casual lunch stop en route — premium soda (traditional Costa Rican restaurant) in Dominical featuring casado, patacones, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort beachside grill — whole grilled lobster, grilled vegetables, coconut rice, passion fruit sorbet dessert

day_by_day.notes: The drive back from the Osa Peninsula is scenic but long — plan for rest stops. If budget allows, a private charter flight from Puerto Jiménez back to the nearest airstrip is a more comfortable option and saves approximately 2 hours. Confirm whale-watching availability seasonally.

day_by_day.morning: Private departure from Aegean Bliss Resort via luxury ground transfer toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3.5–4 hours). Enjoy a scenic drive through the Central Valley highlands. Upon arrival, check into a premium lodge near La Fortuna (Nayara Springs or The Springs Resort & Spa recommended — both offer private hot spring plunge pools).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Arenal Volcano Hike and Hot Springs Soak experience — trek across ancient lava fields and through secondary rainforest on the volcano's flanks with a certified naturalist guide. Observe the dramatic volcanic landscape and learn about Arenal's geological history. Conclude with a private soak in natural thermal hot springs fed by the volcano's geothermal activity.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the lodge's premium restaurant with views of Arenal Volcano (often illuminated dramatically at night). Afterward, enjoy the private hot spring pools under a canopy of stars — one of Costa Rica's most magical experiences.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast from Aegean Bliss Resort for the road, or stop at a premium café in San José en route
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in La Fortuna — Restaurante Nene's or Don Rufino, known for quality Costa Rican cuisine
meals.dinner: Nayara Springs lodge restaurant — elevated Costa Rican cuisine: plantain soup, slow-braised short rib, local cheese board, Costa Rican coffee crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: This is the start of a multi-night stay in the Arenal region. The Arenal Volcano is classified as active — while eruptions are not expected, always follow guide instructions. The hot springs are naturally heated and extremely relaxing; bring a swimsuit. Nayara Springs is adults-only and one of the finest luxury properties in Costa Rica.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboard tour on Lake Arenal — the country's largest lake offers stunning reflections of the volcano at dawn. Spot kingfishers, herons, and ospreys along the shoreline. Return to the lodge for a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — transfer to the Monteverde region (approximately 2–2.5 hours from Arenal, or take the scenic Lake Arenal boat crossing to save time). Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits, with cables stretching over 1km and platforms suspended high above the forest floor.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming town of Santa Elena near Monteverde — visit a premium chocolate or coffee tasting experience at a local artisan producer. Enjoy dinner at a top Monteverde restaurant before returning to the Arenal lodge.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — fresh tropical buffet, specialty Costa Rican coffee, eggs to order
meals.lunch: Lunch in Monteverde at Café Caburé — artisan chocolate café with gourmet sandwiches, soups, and handmade chocolates
meals.dinner: Celajes Restaurant, Monteverde — creative Costa Rican fusion cuisine with cloud forest views; try the mushroom risotto with local fungi or the grilled guapote fish

day_by_day.notes: The lake crossing from Arenal to Monteverde by boat and jeep is a classic Costa Rican adventure and is more scenic and faster than the road route — arrange through the lodge concierge. The zip-line canopy tour requires closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing. Monteverde can be misty and cooler than the coast — bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Guided early morning walk through the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve — one of the most pristine cloud forests in the world. With a naturalist guide, search for the resplendent quetzal (February is an excellent month for sightings), emerald toucanets, golden-browed chlorophonias, and glass frogs. The misty forest at dawn is truly otherworldly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a premium organic coffee and cacao farm near Monteverde for an immersive farm-to-cup experience — learn about sustainable agriculture practices, participate in coffee processing, and enjoy a private cupping session. Return to Arenal lodge via the scenic lake route.
day_by_day.evening: Private couples' spa treatment at the Nayara Springs spa — volcanic clay wraps, hot stone massage, and aromatherapy using locally sourced botanicals. Dinner at the lodge's intimate private dining experience — a chef's table set beside your private hot spring pool.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before the cloud forest walk — fruit, yogurt, granola, coffee
meals.lunch: Farm lunch at the coffee/cacao estate — traditional Costa Rican spread prepared with farm-grown ingredients
meals.dinner: Nayara Springs private chef's table dinner — personalized multi-course tasting menu prepared exclusively for your party beside your private plunge pool; champagne and wine pairing included

day_by_day.notes: The resplendent quetzal is one of the most sought-after birds in the Americas — February coincides with the beginning of their breeding season, making sightings more likely. Pre-book the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve entrance; visitor numbers are limited daily. The private chef's table experience at Nayara requires advance reservation — book through the lodge concierge immediately upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in the Arenal region. Optional white-water rafting on the Río Toro (Class III–IV) for thrill-seekers, or a tranquil morning hanging bridges walk through the rainforest canopy at the Mistico Arenal Hanging Bridges Park — a gentler alternative offering excellent wildlife viewing. Breakfast at the lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury ground transfer back toward the Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 3.5–4 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Costa Rican highlands, stopping at a premium roadside viewpoint café in the Central Valley for coffee and local pastries.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a sunset swim in the Pacific Ocean followed by cocktails at the beach bar. Dinner at the resort's rooftop restaurant for panoramic ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Lodge farewell breakfast — full tropical spread, eggs, gallo pinto, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Premium café stop en route — artisan coffee, empanadas, local cheeses, fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort rooftop restaurant — Pacific catch of the day, grilled octopus salad, local craft beer or premium cocktail pairing, tres leches cake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The hanging bridges at Mistico Park are suitable for all fitness levels and provide a completely different perspective of the rainforest canopy compared to zip-lining — ideal for photography. Confirm return transfer timing with the Arenal lodge concierge the evening prior. Pack bags the night before to allow for an early, relaxed departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day at Aegean Bliss Resort — a premium leisure morning. Sleep in, enjoy a champagne breakfast on your private terrace, then spend the morning on a private guided surf lesson or kayak tour along the coastline arranged by the resort's water sports team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a full afternoon at the resort spa — choose from a menu of signature treatments including a volcanic mineral body scrub, deep tissue massage, and rejuvenating facial. Afterward, lounge by the infinity pool with chilled cocktails and light snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner — reserve the resort's exclusive private beach dining experience: a table set directly on the sand, torches lit, personalized menu crafted by the executive chef, and a dedicated sommelier for wine pairings. Toast to an extraordinary Costa Rica adventure as the waves roll in under a star-filled sky.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on private terrace — fresh pastries, smoked salmon, tropical fruits, sparkling rosé
meals.lunch: Poolside gourmet lunch — lobster roll, truffle fries, fresh coconut, premium sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — five-course bespoke menu: tuna tartare, hearts of palm soup, grilled whole lobster, filet mignon, and a decadent chocolate and passion fruit dessert tower; premium wine and champagne pairing

day_by_day.notes: The private beach dinner experience is the signature farewell event — book this through the resort concierge at least 3 days in advance as it requires special setup and chef coordination. This is also an ideal day for any final souvenir shopping at the resort boutique or nearby artisan markets. Begin packing this evening for the next day's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the beach — a quiet, reflective moment to absorb the beauty of Costa Rica one last time. Enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort. Complete checkout formalities — the resort's concierge team will handle luggage and ensure a seamless departure experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury airport transfer via chauffeured SUV to the airport. Arrive with ample time for international departure. If the flight departs in the afternoon or evening, the resort may arrange a late checkout or a comfortable day-use room for freshening up before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica — carry with you extraordinary memories of cloud forests, volcanic landscapes, Pacific sunsets, and some of the most biodiverse wildlife on the planet. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full gourmet spread; savor every last bite of gallo pinto and tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport lounge — ceviche, fresh juice, café con leche
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm flight details and airport transfer timing the evening before. Request a late checkout (typically until 14:00 or later for premium guests) to avoid rushing. The resort concierge can arrange duty-free purchases, currency exchange, and any last-minute needs. Ensure all wildlife-related purchases (if any) comply with CITES regulations — Costa Rica strictly prohibits the export of certain biological materials. Consider leaving a gratuity for outstanding resort and guide staff.
